lexSnapshot.derivativeNote: وَسَقَ is in the derivative form: وَسَقَ
lexSnapshot.rootDefinitionHtml:
و/س/ق   w–s–q a camel’s load, a dry measure of a certain capacity; a flock of birds, a herd of animals; to load, a beast of burden; to cover up (of night), to rise up in the sky (of the moon), to become a full moon, to shine upon the land below; to gather together, to be complete, to be in perfect order. Of this root, 2 forms, وَسَقَ wasaqa and اتَّسَقَ ʾittasaqa, occur 1 time each in the Qur’an
.
lexSnapshot.mainDefinitionHtml:
وَسَقَ wasaqa i [v. trans.] to gather together; to cover; to span; to enshroud

(84:17) وَاللَّيْلِ وَمَا وَسَقَ by the night and all that it covers.

entries.label: اتَّسَقَ
entries.definitionHtml:
اتَّسَقَ ʾittasaqa [v. VIII, intrans.] to reach fullness, to realise full potential; to become in good order

(84:18) وَالْقَمَرِ إِذَا اتَّسَقَ by the moon when it becomes full.
